III p367.text: And so the way it should have been put is: Laughter comes from a man’s idea of his own superiority.

transcription.reason: No reliably accessible machine transcription of this exact publisher-authorized preview is available to the kit; the maker directly read the full sentence on the Cambridge page image and preserves its words, capitalization and punctuation.
transcription.original_text: And so the way it should have been put is: Laughter comes from a man’s idea of his own superiority.

III p367.alignment: This complete sentence corresponds to the French sentence. The generic a man and his make the subject grammatically masculine in English, whereas French sa does not specify gender and the following example includes Virginie; a generic human reading retains the sense but the potential narrowing is disclosed.

V p374.text: From the artistic point of view, the comic is an imitation; the grotesque, a creation. The comic is an imitation mixed with a certain degree of creative capacity, or, in other words, of artistic ideality.

transcription.reason: The maker directly read both complete sentences on the Cambridge page image; no reliably accessible machine transcription of this exact authorized preview is available to the kit.
transcription.original_text: From the artistic point of view, the comic is an imitation; the grotesque, a creation. The comic is an imitation mixed with a certain degree of creative capacity, or, in other words, of artistic ideality.

V p374.alignment: Both complete sentences preserve the contrast between comic imitation and grotesque creation and the mixture of a creative faculty or artistic ideality. The English certain degree of creative capacity makes degree explicit where the French says a certain creative faculty.

V p375.text: From now on I shall refer to the grotesque as the absolute comic, in contrast to the ordinary comic, which I shall call the significative comic. The significative comic speaks a language that is clearer, easier for the common man to understand, and especially easier to analyse, its element being obviously double: art and the moral idea; but the absolute comic, coming as it does much closer to nature, appears as a unity that must be grasped intuitively.
